planting.note: Plant bare-root seedlings in late winter while dormant in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, then graft a desired English walnut variety onto the young rootstock; Paradox is a vigorous hybrid understock, not grown for its own nuts.

directions: Plant bare-root seedlings in late winter while dormant in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, then graft a desired English walnut variety onto the young rootstock; Paradox is a vigorous hybrid understock, not grown for its own nuts. A hybrid between Northern California black walnut and English walnut, first noticed for its unusually vigorous, fast growth compared to either parent species, it has become the standard rootstock for commercial English walnut production in California, imparting notably greater vigor, earlier bearing, and better tolerance of a range of soil conditions than seedling English walnut rootstock. Traditional seedling-grown Paradox is genetically variable since it arises from open-pollinated crosses, which has driven development of named clonal selections such as RX1 and VX211 for more uniform, disease-resistant performance. Graft a desired named English walnut variety onto young rootstock in late winter, and give the resulting tree ample permanent space, since walnut on Paradox rootstock grows into a very large, long-lived tree.

planting.note: Plant clonally propagated rootstock liners in late winter while dormant in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, then graft a desired English walnut variety onto the young rootstock; RX1 is a disease-resistant clonal understock, not grown for its own nuts.

directions: Plant clonally propagated rootstock liners in late winter while dormant in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, then graft a desired English walnut variety onto the young rootstock; RX1 is a disease-resistant clonal understock, not grown for its own nuts. Developed by the University of California walnut breeding program as a clonally propagated hybrid rootstock, it was bred specifically for strong resistance to Phytophthora root and crown rot and to lesion nematode, two of the most damaging soil-borne problems limiting walnut orchard longevity on the traditional seedling Paradox rootstock, while offering the genetic uniformity that open-pollinated seedling Paradox lacks. Its combination of disease resistance and vigor comparable to Paradox has made it an increasingly popular modern choice for new commercial walnut plantings on disease-prone or replant sites. Graft a desired named English walnut variety onto young rootstock in late winter, and expect vigorous, disease-resistant growth well suited to sites with a history of walnut root disease.

planting.note: Plant clonally propagated rootstock liners in late winter while dormant in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, then graft a desired English walnut variety onto the young rootstock; VX211 is a vigorous clonal understock with improved crown gall tolerance, not grown for its own nuts.

directions: Plant clonally propagated rootstock liners in late winter while dormant in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, then graft a desired English walnut variety onto the young rootstock; VX211 is a vigorous clonal understock with improved crown gall tolerance, not grown for its own nuts. Another clonally propagated hybrid rootstock selection from the University of California walnut breeding program, it combines strong vigor and good tolerance of a range of soil conditions with improved resistance to crown gall compared to traditional seedling Paradox rootstock, while offering the propagation uniformity that clonal selections provide over genetically variable seedling stock. It has become a favored alternative to RX1 on sites where crown gall rather than Phytophthora or nematode pressure is the primary soil-borne concern. Graft a desired named English walnut variety onto young rootstock in late winter, and expect vigorous, uniform growth with improved resilience against crown gall infection.

planting.note: Plant container-grown clonal rootstock liners after last frost in well-drained soil in full sun, then graft a desired avocado variety onto the young rootstock; Dusa is a Phytophthora-tolerant clonal understock, not grown for its own fruit.

directions: Plant container-grown clonal rootstock liners after last frost in well-drained soil in full sun, then graft a desired avocado variety onto the young rootstock; Dusa is a Phytophthora-tolerant clonal understock, not grown for its own fruit. A South African clonal avocado rootstock selection bred specifically for strong tolerance of Phytophthora root rot, one of the most economically damaging avocado diseases worldwide, while also imparting good vigor, high yields, and reasonably good tolerance of some soil salinity to the grafted variety. Its clonal propagation gives far more uniform performance across an orchard than older seedling avocado rootstocks, whose disease tolerance and vigor vary unpredictably from tree to tree. Graft a desired named avocado variety onto young rootstock, provide excellent drainage despite the improved Phytophthora tolerance, since no avocado rootstock is fully immune, and expect vigorous, productive growth in warm, frost-free climates.
